title: Karoline Leavitt to Step Down as White House Press Secretary at End of August
detail: President Trump announced on Truth Social on August 12, 2026 that White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, 28, will leave her role at the end of the month to spend more time with her two young children, including a daughter born in May. Leavitt, the youngest press secretary in history, said she 'cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required' by the job. Trump praised her as 'one of the best White House Press Secretaries in the History of the Office' and said she would remain a 'top outside advisor' and influential GOP voice ahead of the midterms. No successor was named.

media.caption: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who will step down at the end of August 2026

title: White House Credits 'Trump Effect' as Homicides Fall 17% Nationally in First Half of 2026
detail: Data from 66 law enforcement agencies compiled by the Major Cities Chiefs Association, publicized by the White House on August 12, 2026, showed homicides in major US cities fell to 2,162 in the first half of 2026 from 2,611 in the same period of 2025 — a roughly 17% drop — with rape, robbery, and aggravated assault also declining. The White House attributed the trend to a 'Trump effect.' Crime analysts said 2026 is on pace for the lowest recorded US murder rate, but noted the decline began in 2022, years before Trump returned to office, and a subsequent Washington Post analysis (Aug 15) found crime 'has been falling for years' independent of Trump-era policy.

media.caption: Homicides fell 17% nationally in the first half of 2026; the White House calls the trend a 'Trump effect'
